Amumu.watch: Amumu Q Bandage Toss stops at the first target, so dodge it with a minion or jungle monster between you and Amumu. After it catches you, you keep taking damage from Amumu W Despair, which deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t stay near him for long.
Amumu.build: Choose Mercury's Treads before Plated Steelcaps to mitigate Amumu’s magic damage and stun. Graves’s magic resistance decreases as he levels, so shore it up. If you have to attack Amumu directly, also get armor penetration to deal with Amumu E Tantrum’s physical damage reduction.
Amumu.fight: After dodging Amumu Q Bandage Toss, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from an angle with no units in between. Amumu E Tantrum comes back faster the more basic attacks he takes, so avoid extended fights against him.
Amumu.laning: Gank when the enemy has pushed past the lane center and an ally can lock them down. Close the angle with Graves E Quickdraw, then throw Graves W Smoke Screen in their escape path. If the angle is uncertain, don’t force it; clear camps to gain levels and gold.
Amumu.combo: If Amumu Q Bandage Toss is down, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Once you’re close, cut off his vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and follow up with Graves Q End of the Line. If he has his back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line against it for a quick explosion. Finish with Graves R Collateral Damage, accounting for the knockback that follows the cast.
Amumu.escape: Look for an opening while Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down. Amumu has no skill that creates distance on his own, so use Graves E Quickdraw to engage and fight; if needed, close the gap with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Amumu.phase: In the mid game, secure that advantage with objectives and vision. Graves gets stronger as he stacks, giving him the advantage later, but his range is short and his magic resistance is low in the late game, so avoid being caught first.

Brand.watch: If Brand’s Blaze is applied, Brand Q Sear stuns you, and repeated hits from his abilities stack Blaze until it explodes. Dodge Brand W Pillar of Flame and Brand Q Sear first. If you’re ablaze, dodge the Q projectile from behind minions.
Brand.build: Since the enemy’s damage is mostly magic, choose Mercury's Treads. Graves’s magic resistance decreases as he levels, so shore up your magic resistance rather than your armor.
Brand.laning: Try to gank when Brand has pushed past the lane center and an ally can lock him down. Keep clear of burning minions, since Brand E Conflagration can spread from them. If the gank angle is uncertain, clear camps to grow stronger.
Brand.combo: Once Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Throw Graves W Smoke Screen in his escape path, then hit him with Graves Q End of the Line. If Brand has his back to a wall, fire Q against it for a quick explosion, then finish with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility, so the moment after he uses Brand W Pillar of Flame is your chance to engage. If you’re ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear first, then go in with Graves E Quickdraw.
Brand.phase: You’ll be better positioned to damage Brand as you grow stronger, but be careful not to get caught first in the late game because of your short range and low magic resistance. Secure objective and vision advantages in the early and mid game.
Brand.teamfight: Don’t initiate from the front. After your allies draw attention, approach Brand from the flank with Graves E Quickdraw. Spread out from allies so Brand E Conflagration and Brand R Pyroclasm don’t spread between you, and position so no units block your basic attacks.

Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush dashes in, stuns, and lowers your armor, so watch for her engage and dodge with Graves E Quickdraw. Briar E Chilling Scream heals her and can stun enemies knocked into a wall, so don’t stand with your back to one when she starts charging it. If Briar R Certain Death marks you as prey, she gains resistances and movement speed and will chase you, so move toward your allies and fight her together.
Briar.build: Build armor first to counter Briar’s main damage. Keep using Graves E Quickdraw’s armor stacks by landing basic attacks during fights. If duels drag on because of Briar P Crimson Curse, Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack, and the healing from Briar E Chilling Scream, build resistances first, then fit Executioner's Calling between core items.
Briar.fight: Avoid trades where Briar Q Head Rush hits and reduces your armor. Use Graves E Quickdraw to position for close-range basic attacks that aren’t blocked by units. While Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack is active, she chases the nearest enemy, so fight from the side with your frontline and slow her with Graves W Smoke Screen. Just damaging Briar can delay her next jungle route, so you don’t have to risk a kill.
Briar.laning: Clear camps quickly. If the gank angle is uncertain, cast Graves Q End of the Line against a camp wall to gain levels and gold. Set up vision to prepare for Briar’s early ganks, and don’t linger in the middle of a lane where you lack vision. When ganking, check that the enemy has pushed forward and an ally can lock them down, then approach with Graves E Quickdraw and place Graves W Smoke Screen in their escape path.
Briar.combo: Approach with Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading to load one shell, then land close-range basic attacks from an angle with no units in between. Cut off vision with Graves W Smoke Screen, then use Graves Q End of the Line. Against Briar with her back to a wall, aim Q at the wall for an instant explosion. Use Graves R Collateral Damage if you need to finish her.
Briar.escape: Don’t go in just because Briar Q Head Rush is down. Check that Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack and Briar R Certain Death are also unavailable, and close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and Graves R Collateral Damage, especially before her ultimate comes back up. If Briar E Chilling Scream is still available, fight from a position where you can avoid being stunned against a wall.
Briar.phase: If you survive the early game, Graves gets stronger as he stacks and gradually gains the advantage in this matchup. Use your early and mid-game strength to secure objectives and vision. In the late game, be careful not to get caught first because of Graves’s short range.
Briar.teamfight: Don’t initiate from the front. After your allies draw Briar’s attention, go in from the flank with Graves E Quickdraw. Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack chases the nearest enemy, so find an angle with no units between you and the backline damage dealers while your frontline faces Briar. If an ally is marked by Briar R Certain Death, fight her together, and use Graves R Collateral Damage from an angle where another enemy is behind your target.

Diana.watch: Diana Q Crescent Strike curves toward you and leaves a mark, so dodge sideways instead of only backing away. If you’re marked, Diana E Lunar Rush may reset, so use Graves E Quickdraw to get out of position. Don’t engage just after Diana activates Diana W Pale Cascade; wait for its orbs and shield to wear off.
Diana.build: Choose Mercury's Treads first. Diana’s damage is mostly magic, so it’s better to build magic resistance than Plated Steelcaps.
Diana.fight: Fight after dodging Diana Q Crescent Strike, or when Diana E Lunar Rush is down without a mark. Close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from an angle with no units in between. Trade after the orbs and shield from Diana W Pale Cascade are gone.
Diana.laning: If the gank angle is uncertain, clear camps. When ganking, check that the enemy has pushed forward and an ally can lock them down.
Diana.combo: After dodging Diana Q Crescent Strike, or when Diana E Lunar Rush is down without a mark, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Place Graves W Smoke Screen in her escape path and hit her with the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line. If she has her back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line against it. Use Graves R Collateral Damage if you need to finish her.
Diana.escape: If Diana uses Diana E Lunar Rush without a mark from Diana Q Crescent Strike, engage while she has no way to dash back out. Slow her with Graves W Smoke Screen, then close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw. If you’re marked, don’t engage; create distance.
Diana.phase: Graves gets stronger as he stacks, so if you survive the early game, the matchup gets more favorable over time. But in the late game, getting caught first is dangerous because of his short range and low magic resistance. Secure your early and mid-game advantages with objectives and vision.
Diana.teamfight: Graves should not initiate from the front. After your allies draw attention, approach the damage dealers from the flank with Graves E Quickdraw. Spread out so multiple allies aren’t pulled in by Diana R Moonfall, and secure vision on the flank’s approach. Once you’re in, position so no units are between you and your target.

Elise.build: Build magic resistance first to counter Elise’s main damage, and choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps. If healing from Elise P Spider Queen prevents you from securing kills, slot Executioner’s Calling between core items.
Elise.fight: Start a fight after dodging Elise E Cocoon or blocking it with a unit. Close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw, get in basic attacks from a position with no unit between you and Elise, then use E again just before reloading to keep attacking.
Elise.laning: Early on, ward and watch for Elise’s ganks. Don’t overpush your lane when Elise is missing. If a gank angle is poor, Graves can gain levels and gold by clearing the jungle quickly; gank when the enemy steps forward and your ally can lock them down.
Elise.combo: After dodging Elise E Cocoon, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Use Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off vision, then hit her with Graves Q End of the Line. If Elise has her back to a wall, aim Q at the wall to make it explode sooner.
Elise.escape: Right after Elise uses Elise Q Neurotoxin / Elise Q Venomous Bite, you may get a chance to close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage. If Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are both on cooldown, turn and fight her.
Elise.phase: Early on, Elise tries to build an advantage through ganks, so avoid giving up kills and hold on. The matchup favors Graves as the game goes on, but in the late game, watch out for getting caught first because of Graves’ short range and low magic resistance.
Elise.teamfight: Don’t engage first from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy’s attention, enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Keep a position where no unit is between you and your target, and avoid getting hit first by Elise E Cocoon.

Ekko.watch: When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of its area to avoid the stun and shield. Also move out of the path of Ekko Q Timewinder as it returns. If an afterimage appears behind Ekko, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so don’t chase recklessly even if he is low.
Ekko.build: Choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps and build magic resistance to prepare for Ekko’s magic damage. If healing from Ekko R Chronobreak makes him hard to kill, slot Executioner’s Calling between core items.
Ekko.fight: Avoid the area of Ekko W Parallel Convergence, then look for a chance when Ekko E Phase Dive is down. Close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and basic attack from an angle with no other unit between you and Ekko. If Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, don’t chase deep to try to kill him in one go.
Ekko.laning: Early on, secure levels and gold by clearing the jungle quickly, and take camps if the gank angle is poor. At camps by a wall, cast Graves Q End of the Line along the wall to clear them. Gank when the enemy is forward in lane and your ally can lock them down: approach with Graves E Quickdraw and place Graves W Smoke Screen along their escape route.
Ekko.combo: Approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land close-range basic attacks. Cut off vision with Graves W Smoke Screen, then hit Ekko with Graves Q End of the Line. If Ekko has his back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line at the wall to make it explode sooner. Using Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading refills a shell so you can keep attacking. When Ekko R Chronobreak is down, look to finish him with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Ekko.escape: Commit after both Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are down. If only Ekko E Phase Dive is down, he can still escape with Ekko R Chronobreak, so check that his remaining mobility is unavailable too. When you get an opening, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage.
Ekko.phase: In the early and mid game, turn objectives and vision into a lasting advantage. Even if the matchup becomes more favorable later, avoid getting caught first because of Graves’ short range and low magic resistance.
Ekko.teamfight: Don’t engage first from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy’s attention, enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. If you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, avoid its area, then look for an opening just after Ekko uses Ekko E Phase Dive to get on you. Keep a position where no other unit is between you and your target.

Evelynn.watch: When you see the mark from Evelynn W Allure, back away before you are charmed and alert your allies. At low health, watch out for the execute damage from Evelynn R Last Caress.
Evelynn.fight: When fighting, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from an angle where units won’t block your shots. The window to chase is after Evelynn R Last Caress is down.
Evelynn.laning: If the gank angle is poor, use Graves’ fast jungle clear to farm camps and gain levels and gold. Ward near Evelynn’s jungle camps where she might start a fight to track her position. When ganking, approach with Graves E Quickdraw when the enemy is forward in lane and your ally can lock them down, then throw Graves W Smoke Screen along their escape route.
Evelynn.combo: Approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. If you can use E again just before reloading, refill a shell and keep attacking. Once close, cut off vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and hit Evelynn with Graves Q End of the Line. If Evelynn has her back to a wall, aim at the wall to make it explode sooner. When Evelynn R Last Caress is down, finish her with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Evelynn.escape: Back away before the mark from Evelynn W Allure matures to avoid the charm. Don’t engage just because Evelynn E Whiplash is down; wait until Evelynn R Last Caress is also down and look for her before it comes back. Then close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and Graves R Collateral Damage.
Evelynn.phase: In the early and mid game, turn objectives and vision into an advantage, and make use of your scaling if you survive the early game. In the late game, be careful not to get caught first because of Graves’ short range and low magic resistance.
Evelynn.teamfight: Graves shouldn’t start the fight. Once your allies draw the enemy’s attention, enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Evelynn targets backline damage dealers, so move where your team has vision and save your allies’ immobilizing effects for her. After Evelynn engages, cut off vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and attack from a position where no unit is between you and your target.

Gragas.watch: If Gragas E Body Slam knocks you up, it can lead into the explosion from Gragas Q Barrel Roll, so move outside the barrel’s radius when you see it. When Gragas starts drinking with Gragas W Drunken Rage, he takes reduced damage, so delay your burst briefly. When Gragas has Gragas R Explosive Cask ready, don’t stand with an enemy turret or the enemy team behind you.
Gragas.build: If healing from Gragas P Happy Hour makes you miss kills, slot Executioner’s Calling between core items. Gragas’ damage is mostly magic, so choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps and build magic resistance. Since Gragas has fairly high armor, also consider penetration to deal physical damage.
Gragas.fight: Right after Gragas uses Gragas E Body Slam, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw. After the damage reduction from Gragas W Drunken Rage ends, land close-range basic attacks and Graves Q End of the Line from an angle with no other unit between you and Gragas. Using Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading adds a shell so you can keep attacking.
Gragas.laning: Look to gank when Gragas is past the middle of the lane and your ally has a way to lock him down. Close the angle with Graves E Quickdraw, then throw Graves W Smoke Screen along his escape route. If the angle is poor, don’t chase recklessly; gain levels and gold by casting Graves Q End of the Line along the wall at camps by a wall.
Gragas.combo: When Gragas E Body Slam is down, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land close-range basic attacks. Follow up with Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off vision and Graves Q End of the Line, but wait until the damage reduction from Gragas W Drunken Rage ends before bursting him. If Gragas has his back to a wall, aim at the wall to make Graves Q End of the Line explode sooner.
Gragas.escape: The window to engage is right after Gragas uses Gragas E Body Slam. Close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw then, but avoid chasing deep unless you can secure the kill, since hitting Gragas E Body Slam reduces its cooldown.
Gragas.phase: In the early and mid game, turn Graves’ fast jungle clear and skirmishing strength into objective and vision advantages. Gragas’ sustained damage weakens as the game goes on, improving the matchup, but in the late game, watch out for getting caught first because Graves has short range and low magic resistance.
Gragas.teamfight: Don’t let your backline stand alone within range of Gragas E Body Slam, and avoid narrow passages and unwarded brush. Graves shouldn’t engage first from the front; once your allies draw the enemy’s attention, dive in from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Attack from a position where no unit is between you and your target. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you, prioritize getting outside the radius of Gragas Q Barrel Roll over counterattacking.

Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm enters after channeling, so when you see the cast, try to interrupt it with the slow from Graves W Smoke Screen. If you can’t interrupt it, get out of range and wait for the duration to end. If Fiddlesticks has been out of sight for a long time, suspect an ambush from a bush, and don’t pass close to a Scarecrow Effigy before checking it.
Fiddlesticks.fight: Use Graves E Quickdraw to close the gap and attack at close range from an angle where units won’t block your basic attacks. Don’t stay close and let Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest run its full course, since that puts you at a disadvantage in both healing and cooldowns.
Fiddlesticks.laning: Try to gank when the opponent has pushed past the center of the lane and your ally can hold them. Close the angle with Graves E Quickdraw, then throw Graves W Smoke Screen in their escape path. If the gank angle is uncertain, clear camps to gain levels and gold.
Fiddlesticks.combo: Approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land close-range basic attacks, place Graves W Smoke Screen in the opponent’s escape path, then follow up with Graves Q End of the Line. If you use Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading, one shell is added to the magazine so you can keep attacking. If Fiddlesticks has his back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line toward the wall, and use Graves R Collateral Damage to finish him.
Fiddlesticks.escape: Look for an opportunity to go in with Graves E Quickdraw while Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm is on cooldown. If Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap are on cooldown, the risk of being hit by fear and silence is lower, making it a good time to approach. If Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm has already started, use Graves E Quickdraw to get out of range, and use the knockback from Graves R Collateral Damage to escape if needed.
Fiddlesticks.phase: In the mid game, secure your lead with objectives and vision. Graves gets stronger as he stacks, so in this matchup you become more favored as the game goes on if you survive the early game. In the late game, be careful not to get caught first because of your short range and low magic resistance.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest, E Reap, and R Crowstorm all deal area damage, so spread out from your allies and don’t group together in narrow, unwarded passages. Secure vision in bushes and approaches near objectives to watch for Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm ambushes. After your allies draw the opponents’ attention, enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw and attack from a position where no units are between you and your target.

JarvanIV.laning: If the gank angle is uncertain, cast Graves Q End of the Line against a camp wall to farm, and gank when the opponent has pushed up and your ally can hold them.
JarvanIV.combo: Follow with Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off vision, then cast Graves Q End of the Line. If the opponent has their back to a wall, aim it at the wall for a quick explosion.
JarvanIV.phase: If you survive the early game, Graves becomes relatively favored as he grows stronger with stacks, but in the late game, manage your vision and positioning so you don’t get caught first.
JarvanIV.teamfight: When you get onto a damage dealer, position yourself so no other unit is between you and your target.

Ivern.watch: If you’re rooted by Ivern Q Rootcaller, Ivern’s allies can dash in, so avoid it by keeping minions or terrain between you and Ivern before he fires. Ivern E Triggerseed leaves a slow after it explodes on its target, so don’t engage immediately. If Ivern R Daisy! starts attacking you, reposition to interrupt her consecutive attacks and knock-up.
Ivern.build: Ivern’s damage is mostly magic, so choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps. Graves’ magic resistance decreases as he scales, so make up for it with your boots. If you often die when Ivern’s crowd control lets his allies follow up, consider tenacity first.
Ivern.fight: Right after dodging Ivern Q Rootcaller, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and follow with basic attacks. If the target already has Ivern E Triggerseed on them, engage after the shield explodes. Target the ally Ivern shields first instead of chasing him deep.
Ivern.laning: Don’t casually walk beside newly created Ivern W Brushmaker. If the gank angle is uncertain, cast Graves Q End of the Line against camp walls to clear quickly and gain levels and gold.
Ivern.combo: When Ivern Q Rootcaller is on cooldown, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land close-range basic attacks, place Graves W Smoke Screen in the escape path, then hit with Graves Q End of the Line. If the opponent has their back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line at the wall to hit them with the explosion sooner. Use Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading to keep up your basic attacks, and finish with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Ivern.escape: Ivern Q Rootcaller is both Ivern’s mobility and his root, so the moment after you bait it out is your window to engage. Close the gap then with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage. If the target has Ivern E Triggerseed on them, engage after the explosion.
Ivern.phase: In the early and mid game, secure your lead with objectives and vision. In this matchup, surviving the early game makes things increasingly favorable for Graves, but in the late game, be careful not to get caught first because of your short range and low magic resistance.
Ivern.teamfight: Don’t initiate from the front; wait for your allies to draw attention, then approach from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Target the ally protected by Ivern E Triggerseed after it explodes, and position yourself so no units are between you and the target. If Ivern R Daisy! blocks your path, don’t waste Graves Q End of the Line on an opponent behind Daisy; reposition for a better angle.

Hecarim.watch: The longer Hecarim runs with Hecarim E Devastating Charge, the greater its damage and knockback, so if Hecarim starts running from a distance, cut off his vision with Graves W Smoke Screen or move toward your allies. While Hecarim W Spirit of Dread is active, he heals from damage dealt around him, so don’t fight him for long; back out of range. Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows can fear multiple people, so spread out from your allies in team fights.
Hecarim.build: Build armor first against Hecarim’s main damage sources, Hecarim Q Rampage and Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If healing from Hecarim W Spirit of Dread is stopping you from securing kills, fit Executioner’s Calling between core items.
Hecarim.fight: When a fight starts, slow Hecarim with Graves W Smoke Screen to reduce both his ability to engage and his damage. Don’t use Graves E Quickdraw to flee without thinking; use it to engage and build armor stacks.
Hecarim.laning: If the gank angle is uncertain, cast Graves Q End of the Line against a wall to clear camps and gain levels and gold.
Hecarim.combo: When Hecarim approaches, slow him first with Graves W Smoke Screen and cut off his vision. When you get another chance to engage, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and attack from an angle where units won’t block your basic attacks, then fire Graves Q End of the Line at the wall when Hecarim has his back to it. Use Graves R Collateral Damage if you need to finish him.
Hecarim.escape: Don’t go in just because Hecarim E Devastating Charge is on cooldown. Look for a window before Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows is back, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw, and use Graves R Collateral Damage to chase or create distance if needed.
Hecarim.phase: When Graves is strong in the early and mid game, secure your lead with objectives and vision. This matchup favors you more as you scale, but in the late game, be careful not to get caught first because of your short range.
Hecarim.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows doesn’t hit several of you at once. Instead of initiating from the front, wait for your allies to draw Hecarim’s attention, then engage from the side and use Graves W Smoke Screen to slow his approach.

Jax.watch: Jax E Counter Strike negates basic attacks and stuns in an area when reactivated. Stop auto-attacking while it’s active and move out of stun range. Save Graves E Quickdraw for when you need to create distance.
Jax.build: Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so account for both armor and magic resistance. If the enemy’s damage is mostly magic, choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on your max health, and Jax P Relentless Assault increases his attack speed, so reducing his attack speed can be effective instead of only building health.
Jax.fight: Trade briefly instead of fighting long enough for Jax P Relentless Assault to stack. When Jax E Counter Strike activates, stop auto-attacking and back away. Once it ends, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and attack.
Jax.laning: Jax Q Leap Strike can use units as a stepping stone, so don’t stand close to a minion wave. If a gank opportunity is unclear, farm the jungle quickly to gain levels and gold.
Jax.combo: After Jax E Counter Strike ends, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and auto-attack from an angle with no units between you and Jax. At close range, block his vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and hit him with Graves Q End of the Line. Just before reloading, use Graves E Quickdraw to load one shell and keep attacking.
Jax.escape: The moment after Jax Q Leap Strike is a chance to close the distance. If Jax E Counter Strike’s stun has also been used, go in and attack with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage.
Jax.phase: Graves can gain an advantage as he scales, but getting caught first is dangerous in the late game. Fight while keeping vision and objectives under control.
Jax.teamfight: When Jax activates E Counter Strike and jumps in, spread out and wait out its duration so you aren’t all hit by the area stun. Graves should not engage first; wait for an ally to draw attention, then dive in from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Keep an angle with no other units between you and your target.

Karthus.watch: Karthus Q Lay Waste deals more damage when it hits you alone, so watch its warning area and dodge. Karthus W Wall of Pain reduces magic resistance and slows, so go around the wall. Karthus R Requiem hits regardless of distance, so keep enough health to survive it even after a fight. Karthus P Death Defied lets him cast spells after he dies, so move away from his corpse immediately after a kill.
Karthus.build: Choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps. Karthus Q Lay Waste, E Defile, and R Requiem all deal magic damage, so build magic resistance, but prioritize avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain and quickly leaving the area of Karthus E Defile.
Karthus.fight: Close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and land auto-attacks from an angle with no units in the way. Don’t stay in Karthus E Defile for long.
Karthus.laning: When ganking, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and throw Graves W Smoke Screen along the escape route if the enemy has pushed past lane center and an ally can hold them in place. If the angle is unclear, clear camps to gain levels and gold.
Karthus.combo: Approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land auto-attacks from a position where units won’t block them. Then block Karthus’s vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and follow up with Graves Q End of the Line. If Karthus has his back to a wall, hit the wall with Graves Q End of the Line to land the explosion sooner. Finish with Graves R Collateral Damage, and if you get the kill, move away from his corpse immediately.
Karthus.escape: Karthus has no ability to create distance on his own, so go in with Graves E Quickdraw when you can approach without walking through Karthus W Wall of Pain. Dodge the warning area of Karthus Q Lay Waste, then close the distance. After using Graves E Quickdraw, stay on him with auto-attacks to create a chance to use it again.
Karthus.phase: In the mid game, use Graves’s strong period to secure an advantage with objectives and vision. Graves gets stronger as he stacks, but be careful not to get caught first in the late game because of his short range and low magic resistance.
Karthus.teamfight: Graves should not start the fight. Wait for an ally to draw attention, then enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw and stay close to the enemy damage dealers. Don’t remain in Karthus E Defile for long, and even if you kill Karthus, move away from his corpse immediately while Karthus P Death Defied is active. Keep an angle with no other units blocking your auto-attacks.

Khazix.watch: Kha’Zix Q Taste Their Fear deals much more damage when you’re isolated, so stay near allies or minions. If Kha’Zix disappears with R Void Assault, don’t chase to find him; throw Graves Q End of the Line along his likely entry path. Secure vision in bushes to watch for the bonus damage and slow from Kha’Zix P Unseen Threat.
Khazix.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Kha’Zix Q Taste Their Fear, W Void Spike, and E Leap. If Kha’Zix sustains through fights with W Void Spike, fit Executioner’s Calling between core items.
Khazix.fight: Don’t fight while isolated. Stay near allies and bait Kha’Zix into using E Leap. Right after Kha’Zix goes in with E Leap, use Graves E Quickdraw to adjust your distance and follow with auto-attacks. Keeping up your auto-attacks during the fight can give you a chance to use Graves E Quickdraw again.
Khazix.laning: Make the most of fast jungle clears early, and if a gank opportunity is unclear, farm camps to gain levels and gold. Secure vision in river and jungle entrance bushes so Kha’Zix’s position is harder to read. When ganking, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and throw Graves W Smoke Screen along the escape route if the enemy has pushed forward and an ally can hold them in place.
Khazix.combo: After Kha’Zix E Leap is used, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land auto-attacks. At close range, block his vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and follow up with Graves Q End of the Line. If Kha’Zix has his back to a wall, hit the wall with Graves Q End of the Line to land the explosion sooner.
Khazix.escape: The moment after Kha’Zix uses E Leap to engage is your window to go in. Close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw, and use Graves R Collateral Damage to adjust your distance as well. If Kha’Zix disappears with R Void Assault, stay near allies and wait for him to reappear.
Khazix.phase: If Kha’Zix has two or more evolutions by mid game, stop acting alone. Graves gains an advantage as he builds up defenses, but his short range makes it dangerous to get caught first in the late game, so secure your early and mid-game gains with objectives and vision.
Khazix.teamfight: Group with allies in a narrow area where you have vision to avoid Kha’Zix Q Taste Their Fear’s isolated damage. After an ally draws the enemy’s attention, enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw and find an angle with no units between you and your target. If Kha’Zix disappears with R Void Assault, throw Graves Q End of the Line along his likely entry path and watch for him to reappear near your allies.

Kayn.watch: Dodge the line attack from Kayn W Blade’s Reach. Also watch out for the max-health-based damage from Kayn Q Reaping Slash.
Kayn.build: Build armor first against the main damage from Kayn Q Reaping Slash, W Blade’s Reach, and R Umbral Trespass. If Kayn transforms into a Rhaast and keeps healing, build resistances, then fit Executioner’s Calling between core items.
Kayn.fight: Pressure early skirmishes and objective fights while Kayn is weak before transforming. If you’ve dodged Kayn W Blade’s Reach and Kayn R Umbral Trespass is unavailable, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and follow with auto-attacks from an angle with no units in the way. If Kayn enters a wall with E Shadow Step, damage him while he’s inside to shorten its duration.
Kayn.laning: If a gank opportunity is unclear, bounce Graves Q End of the Line off a camp wall to farm quickly. Pressure Kayn’s jungle route and force objective fights before he transforms, but don’t give him early kills that speed up his transformation. If a warning indicator for Kayn E Shadow Step appears at the edge of a nearby wall, stop fighting and retreat toward your turret.
Kayn.combo: After dodging Kayn W Blade’s Reach, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and follow with auto-attacks. Place Graves W Smoke Screen along the enemy’s escape route and follow with Graves Q End of the Line. If Kayn has his back to a wall, aim at the wall to land the explosion sooner. Using Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading loads one shell so you can keep attacking.
Kayn.escape: Don’t engage just because Kayn Q Reaping Slash is on cooldown. Dodge Kayn W Blade’s Reach and look for an opening before Kayn R Umbral Trespass is available. Close in with Graves E Quickdraw, and use Graves R Collateral Damage to adjust your distance if needed.
Kayn.phase: In the mid game, use Graves’s strong period to secure an advantage with vision and objectives. If you survive the early game and build stacks, you’ll become more favored as the game goes on, but be careful not to let Graves get caught first in the late game.
Kayn.teamfight: Graves should not engage from the front. Wait for an ally to draw attention, then enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Position yourself so no units are between you and your target, then follow with auto-attacks. If Kayn R Umbral Trespass enters an ally, watch where he may emerge around them and be ready for your ally to land crowd control at that moment.

Kindred.watch: If Kindred E Mounting Dread is applied, create distance so you don’t take repeated attacks, or use Graves W Smoke Screen to break vision. Kindred E Mounting Dread is more dangerous when your health is low, so don’t stay close for long in that state.
Kindred.build: Build armor first against Kindred’s main damage from Kindred Q Dance of Arrows and Kindred E Mounting Dread. If healing makes the duel drag on, get resistances first, then fit Executioner’s Calling between core items.
Kindred.fight: Engage before Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy is placed, or look for an opening before Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy comes back. Use Graves E Quickdraw to close the gap and land point-blank basic attacks, keeping no other units between you and Kindred.
Kindred.laning: Slow Kindred P Mark of the Kindred’s growth by taking marked jungle camps first or securing vision nearby. If the gank angle is uncertain, rotate through camps to build a lead in levels and gold. When ganking, approach with Graves E Quickdraw, then throw Graves W Smoke Screen on the escape route.
Kindred.combo: When Kindred’s mobility is down, use Graves E Quickdraw to close in and land basic attacks. Then use Graves W Smoke Screen to break vision and hit with the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line. If Kindred has her back to a wall, aim at the wall. Use Graves R Collateral Damage when you have a chance to finish her.
Kindred.escape: Don’t go in just because Kindred Q Dance of Arrows is down. Your opening is after Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy is also down and before it returns; use Graves E Quickdraw to close the gap during that window.
Kindred.phase: If you survive the early game and keep scaling, the matchup becomes more favorable against Kindred over time. In the late game, watch out for being engaged on first because of your short range. Secure advantages in objectives and vision with your early and midgame strength.
Kindred.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front. Wait for your allies to draw attention, then approach from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Kindred can repeatedly cast Kindred Q Dance of Arrows inside Kindred W Wolf’s Frenzy, so fight while breaking vision with Graves W Smoke Screen. If Kindred R Lamb’s Respite is active, enter the zone to survive and benefit from its healing when it ends.

Lillia.watch: Being hit by Lillia Q Blooming Blows or Lillia E Swirlseed enables the sleep condition for Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, so dodge them even when your health is high. When you see Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! begin, move sideways to avoid the center. If you’re caught by Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, move to safety while you can still act before falling asleep.
Lillia.build: Buy Executioner’s Calling between core items to counter Lillia’s healing. Build magic resistance first against her main damage, and choose Mercury’s Treads instead of Plated Steelcaps. Given the true damage from Lillia Q Blooming Blows and the max-health-based damage from Lillia P Dream-Laden Bough, avoid choices that add a lot of health alone.
Lillia.fight: Close the gap when Lillia misses a skill and has no movement speed stacks. Use Graves E Quickdraw to get close and land basic attacks from a position with no units between you and her. You can keep attacking by using Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading. If Lillia starts Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, move out of the center first.
Lillia.laning: If the gank angle is uncertain, rotate through camps to build a lead in levels and gold. When you don’t know Lillia’s position, don’t pass straight through narrow jungle entrances or river corridors. When ganking, use Graves E Quickdraw to close the angle, then throw Graves W Smoke Screen on the escape route.
Lillia.combo: Right after Lillia misses a skill or uses Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Then break vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and cast Graves Q End of the Line. If Lillia has her back to a wall, aim at the wall to land the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line quickly, then finish her with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Lillia.escape: The moment after you make Lillia use Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! is an opportunity to close the gap. Check whether she has missed a skill and has no movement speed stacks, then go in with Graves E Quickdraw. If you’re caught by Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, don’t engage before falling asleep; move to safety while you can still act.
Lillia.phase: As you scale, your physical damage is effective against Lillia’s low armor, so secure advantages in objectives and vision with your early and midgame strength. In the late game, be careful not to get engaged on first because of Graves’ short range and low magic resistance.
Lillia.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front. Move to the side after your allies draw the enemy’s attention. Save immobilizing crowd control to catch Lillia if she enters from the flank, and when you close in with Graves E Quickdraw, make sure there are no units between you and your target. Break vision with Graves W Smoke Screen, then deal damage with Graves Q End of the Line and basic attacks.

LeeSin.watch: Keep your distance from walls, since Lee Sin can cross them with Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will from beyond your vision. Spread out from allies when Lee Sin R Dragon’s Rage can hit you, since you can take damage together if you’re overlapping.
LeeSin.build: Build armor first against Lee Sin’s main damage from Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and Lee Sin R Dragon’s Rage. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Lee Sin E Tempest / Cripple, but the provided information gives no basis for choosing a specific item.
LeeSin.fight: Don’t accept a head-on duel if you encounter Lee Sin in the early jungle. After Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike misses and Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will is also used, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and keep basic attacking from an angle where units won’t block your attacks. Using Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading lets you add a round to the magazine and keep dealing damage without a break.
LeeSin.laning: If the gank angle is uncertain, build a lead in levels and gold through fast clearing. At camps with walls, fire Graves Q End of the Line along the wall. Gank when the enemy is past the middle of the lane and your ally can lock them down.
LeeSin.combo: After Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike is down and Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will has also been used, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw. Land basic attacks from a position with no units between you and the enemy, place Graves W Smoke Screen on the escape route, then hit with Graves Q End of the Line. If the enemy has their back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line at the wall to land the explosion quickly.
LeeSin.escape: Look for an opening right after Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike misses or is used. If Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will is still available, he can escape with it, so wait until he uses that too before closing the gap with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage.
LeeSin.phase: Avoid head-on duels with Lee Sin early, but scale with Graves’ fast jungle clear. Lee Sin’s strength falls off over time while Graves becomes more favored as he scales, but Graves is vulnerable if caught first in the late game, so choose your entry position carefully.
LeeSin.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front. Wait for your allies to draw attention, then enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw and get onto the damage dealers. Keep a clear line between you and your target so basic attacks aren’t blocked by other units. Spread out appropriately from your allies against Lee Sin R Dragon’s Rage, and keep your back to a wall or your team’s frontline to limit the space Lee Sin has to kick you from behind.

MonkeyKing.watch: You must dodge Wukong E Nimbus Strike from outside its range because it is targeted. Once he gets on you, Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces your armor, and the longer you fight, the more Wukong P Stone Skin builds up its armor and healing, putting you at a disadvantage. When Wukong W Warrior Trickster appears, don’t use skills on the stationary clone; watch the direction the real Wukong moves.
MonkeyKing.build: Build armor first against Wukong’s main damage. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Wukong E Nimbus Strike, and its effectiveness is reduced while your armor is lowered by Wukong Q Crushing Blow. If Wukong P Stone Skin’s healing lets him sustain through the fight, fit Executioner’s Calling between core items.
MonkeyKing.fight: Avoid long duels that let Wukong P Stone Skin stack up; deal damage briefly, then back off. When Wukong closes in with Wukong E Nimbus Strike, break vision and slow him with Graves W Smoke Screen, then use Graves E Quickdraw to manage the distance. Don’t chase the clone and spend your skills before Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down.
MonkeyKing.laning: Look for an angle to fight from outside Wukong E Nimbus Strike’s range, and look to engage when Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down. If the gank angle is uncertain, build a lead in levels and gold through fast clearing. At camps with walls, fire Graves Q End of the Line along the wall to clear faster.
MonkeyKing.combo: After Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks empowered by Graves P New Destiny from an angle with no units between you and the real Wukong. Then break vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and hit with the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line. If you can use Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading, add a round to the magazine to keep dealing damage, then finish with Graves R Collateral Damage.
MonkeyKing.escape: In particular, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage during a window when Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down and you’ve also checked his other mobility and Wukong R Cyclone.
MonkeyKing.phase: If you survive the early game and keep scaling, this matchup becomes more favorable for Graves over time. Secure advantages with objectives and vision in the midgame, and avoid getting engaged on first in the late game because of your short range.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: If Wukong R Cyclone is ready, spread out from your allies and leave room to retreat, accounting for its recast and Wukong W Warrior Trickster’s ultimate as well. Don’t start the fight as Graves; wait for your allies to draw attention, then engage from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Look for a fight or objective right after Wukong R Cyclone is down. When attacking, take a position where no units are between your target and Graves.

MasterYi.watch: Master Yi Q Alpha Strike makes him untargetable while he casts, so look to attack just after he lands. Master Yi E Wuju Style adds true damage to his basic attacks, so don’t stay in close range for long. When Master Yi R Highlander is active, you can’t create distance with the slow from Graves W Smoke Screen.
MasterYi.build: Master Yi E Wuju Style’s true damage can’t be reduced with armor, so build health too. If Master Yi W Meditate’s healing lets him survive a kill attempt, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items.
MasterYi.fight: You can fight Master Yi in the jungle early, while he’s weak. Right after Master Yi Q Alpha Strike is down, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from an angle with no units between you. If Master Yi R Highlander is active, don’t rely on the slow from Graves W Smoke Screen; use your mobility spell to manage the distance.
MasterYi.laning: Graves clears camps quickly, so farm for levels and gold when a gank angle is uncertain. Master Yi is weak in jungle skirmishes and at ganking early, so use chances to encounter him and early objectives to disrupt his growth. Gank when the enemy is past the middle of their lane and your ally has a way to lock them down.
MasterYi.combo: Right after Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks at close range. Follow with Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off his vision and hit him with Graves Q End of the Line. If he’s backed against a wall, aim at the wall to trigger the explosion sooner. Use Graves R Collateral Damage if you need to finish him.
MasterYi.escape: Right after you make Master Yi use Q Alpha Strike is your chance to manage the distance with Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage. While Master Yi R Highlander is active, the slow from Graves W Smoke Screen won’t work, so use your mobility and terrain to get away.
MasterYi.phase: Graves is strong early while Master Yi is weak in the jungle, so gain an advantage through skirmishes and objectives. In the mid game, make the most of Graves’s strength by securing your advantage with vision and objectives. Master Yi also gets stronger late, and Graves is at risk if caught first, but in this matchup Graves has the advantage later on if he builds stacks and survives the early game.
MasterYi.teamfight: Don’t start fights from the front. Wait until your allies draw the enemy’s attention, then enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. If Master Yi gets the first takedown participation, he can quickly stick to his next target, so respond together and don’t let an ally get caught alone. Look for the moment Master Yi W Meditate activates so an ally can interrupt it with immobilizing crowd control.

Nidalee.watch: Nidalee Q Javelin Toss / Takedown’s spear deals more damage the farther it travels, so step out of its path when facing Nidalee from a distance. Also dodge Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce’s traps so you don’t start the fight marked as hunted. If you’re hit by a spear, save Graves E Quickdraw to respond when Nidalee closes in with Pounce.
Nidalee.build: Prioritize Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps and build magic resistance against Nidalee’s damage. If Nidalee E Primal Surge / Swipe’s healing lets her survive a kill attempt, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items.
Nidalee.fight: Start the fight while dodging spears and traps, and close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw right after Nidalee uses W Bushwhack / Pounce. Once you’re close, land basic attacks from an angle with no units in between. Use E just before reloading to keep your attacks going.
Nidalee.laning: Watch for Nidalee W Bushwhack / Pounce’s traps on jungle entrances and in the river. Check for them with a Control Ward or an area-of-effect ability such as Graves Q End of the Line before going in. If a gank angle is uncertain, clear camps for levels and gold; at camps with walls, cast Q against the wall to clear them. Gank when the enemy is far up the lane and your ally can lock them down.
Nidalee.combo: After Nidalee uses W Bushwhack / Pounce, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Follow with Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off her vision and hit her with Graves Q End of the Line. If Nidalee is backed against a wall, cast Q at the wall to land the explosion sooner. Use Graves R Collateral Damage to finish her.
Nidalee.escape: Nidalee has no crowd control, so the moment after she uses W Bushwhack / Pounce is your chance to go in. Close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw, but if you were hit by a spear, save E to respond to Nidalee’s Pounce and Q Takedown. If you’re in danger, cast Graves W Smoke Screen behind you; if needed, use the knockback from Graves R Collateral Damage to escape over a wall.
Nidalee.teamfight: Don’t start fights from the front. Wait until your allies draw the enemy’s attention, then enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Remember where Nidalee stepped out to throw her spear, and look for an angle to engage after she uses W Bushwhack / Pounce. When attacking, position yourself so there are no other units between you and your target.

Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy’s main damage. Don’t spend resources specifically on magic resistance for Poppy alone, and be careful about heavily stacking health because Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on your maximum health.
Poppy.fight: Close the distance after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge is down. In open space, find an angle with no units between you and Poppy to land Graves P New Destiny basic attacks. Don’t stay in the area left by Poppy Q Hammer Shock.
Poppy.laning: Take a position where you aren’t backed against a wall or narrow passage and can avoid the stun from Poppy E Heroic Charge. When Poppy P Iron Ambassador’s shield drops, step on it first to prevent her from getting the shield. If a gank angle is uncertain, clear camps for levels and gold.
Poppy.combo: Once Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge is down, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Follow with Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off her vision and hit her with the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line. Using Graves E Quickdraw just before reloading adds a round to the magazine so you can keep attacking.
Poppy.escape: The moment after you make Poppy use E Heroic Charge is your window to engage. However, if Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, don’t dash near her with Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage; wait for it to end.
Poppy.phase: If you survive the early game, Graves has the advantage over Poppy later on, but you can be caught easily in the late game. Secure an advantage with objectives and vision in the early and mid game.

Nunu.watch: Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! rolls in from a distance and knocks you up, so watch for snowballs coming from out of sight. When you see one, don’t just run backward; dodge toward the path Nunu & Willump came from. If you’re hit by Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, use Graves E Quickdraw to move away before the delayed root lands.
Nunu.build: Fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items to reduce the healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume. Their main damage is magic, so choose Mercury’s Treads over Plated Steelcaps and build magic resistance.
Nunu.fight: After dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and trade damage. Graves’s basic attacks are blocked by units in front of him, so find an angle with no units between you and Nunu & Willump. They can heal with Q Consume, so try to finish them while healing reduction is applied.
Nunu.laning: If a gank angle is uncertain, farm for levels and gold, casting Graves Q End of the Line against camp walls. When ganking, use Graves E Quickdraw to close the angle and throw Graves W Smoke Screen along the enemy’s escape route.
Nunu.combo: After dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from a position where no units block you. Use Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off their vision and cast Graves Q End of the Line; if they’re backed against a wall, aim at the wall to trigger the explosion sooner. Use Graves R Collateral Damage to finish them.
Nunu.escape: Engage after Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! has passed and you’ve dodged the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance, so this is your chance to close in with Graves E Quickdraw. If you can’t interrupt Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero, use the movement from Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage to get out of its area.
Nunu.phase: Late game, watch out for Graves’s short range and low magic resistance so you aren’t caught first.
Nunu.teamfight: Don’t start fights from the front. Wait until your allies draw the enemy’s attention, then enter from the side with Graves E Quickdraw and get beside the enemy carry. Stay positioned so there are no units between Graves and his target. When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero starts, Graves has no way to interrupt it, so don’t force an attack; get out of its area.

Rammus.watch: When Rammus Q Powerball rolls toward you, keep a minion between you and him to avoid the collision. Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is targeted and cannot be dodged once you are in range, so create distance before it reaches you. Rammus R Soaring Slam has a wider area after he gains speed with Rammus Q Powerball, so move away early and avoid the landing spot.
Rammus.build: Prioritize magic resistance against the damage from Rammus Q Powerball, Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl, and Rammus R Soaring Slam. Choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps.
Rammus.fight: Stop attacking and target someone else while Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active. When W ends, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and focus damage on your attacks and the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line. If Rammus needs to be hit for a long time, leave him to an ally with magic damage, true damage, or damage based on maximum health.
Rammus.laning: Graves can clear camps quickly, so farm for levels and gold when the gank angle is uncertain. Keep a minion between you and Rammus Q Powerball in paths where it may appear. Gank when the opponent is pushed forward and your ally can lock them down. Then use Graves E Quickdraw to close the angle and throw Graves W Smoke Screen into their escape route.
Rammus.combo: After Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is down and Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl ends, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and attack. Just before reloading, use Graves E Quickdraw to load a shot, then cut off his vision with Graves W Smoke Screen from close range before using Graves Q End of the Line. Against Rammus with his back to a wall, aim Graves Q End of the Line at the wall to make the explosion hit quickly.
Rammus.escape: If Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is also down, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw. If you are taunted, time it so you can use Graves E Quickdraw as soon as the taunt ends.
Rammus.phase: Use your early and mid-game strength to secure an advantage in camps, objectives, and vision. You grow stronger as you stack, so if you survive the early game, the matchup against Rammus gets more favorable over time. In the late game, though, your range is short and your magic resistance is low, so avoid being caught first.
Rammus.teamfight: Position well outside the expected area of Rammus R Soaring Slam, which begins with Rammus Q Powerball. Do not start the fight from the front; after your allies draw attention, use Graves E Quickdraw from the side to reach the damage dealers. If Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, attack someone else instead of Rammus, and move so no unit is between you and your target.

RekSai.watch: When Rek'Sai Burrows, watch for the moment Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow knocks you up. Avoid walls and narrow paths and move toward open ground; use Graves E Quickdraw to dodge the knock-up as Rek'Sai emerges. If Rek'Sai has recently damaged you, Rek'Sai R Void Rush may come in, so stay close to your allies.
RekSai.build: Prioritize armor against Rek'Sai's main damage. The true damage from Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel cannot be reduced by resistances, and Rek'Sai R Void Rush scales with your maximum health, so be careful about stacking health alone. If healing from Rek'Sai P Fury of the Xer'Sai is preventing a kill, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
RekSai.fight: In the early game, do not give up a kill by meeting Rek'Sai alone where you have no vision. If you dodge the knock-up from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and follow up with attacks. When only Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel is down, Rek'Sai can still escape with Rek'Sai R Void Rush, so check what movement options she has left.
RekSai.laning: If the gank angle is uncertain, fire Graves Q End of the Line against a camp wall and earn levels and gold. If you see an entrance to Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel near a lane or in your own jungle, step on it as you pass to destroy it. Gank when the opponent is past the middle of the lane and your ally has a way to lock them down.
RekSai.combo: As Rek'Sai emerges with Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, use Graves E Quickdraw to dodge the knock-up, then attack at close range from an angle with no other unit between you. Throw Graves W Smoke Screen into her escape route and hit her with Graves Q End of the Line; against Rek'Sai with her back to a wall, aim at the wall to trigger the explosion quickly. Use Graves R Collateral Damage to finish her.
RekSai.escape: The moment after you dodge the knock-up from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow is your chance to engage. Once Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel and Rek'Sai R Void Rush are also down, close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw.
RekSai.phase: The longer the game goes, the more favorable the matchup becomes for Graves, so secure your early and mid-game gains with objectives and vision. In the late game, be careful not to get caught first because Graves has short range.
RekSai.teamfight: Do not start the fight from the front. After your allies draw the opponent's attention, engage from the side or behind with Graves E Quickdraw. Keep attacking from a position where no other unit is between you and the damage dealer. When Rek'Sai chases you, drop Graves W Smoke Screen behind you to disrupt the pursuit, and use the knockback movement from Graves R Collateral Damage to escape.

Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from brush and build Ferocity, so avoid passing beside brush when Rengar is out of sight. When his resource bar is full, Rengar E Bola Strike can root you, so avoid trading and use Graves E Quickdraw after he throws it. When Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt is active, do not travel alone; stay with allies and overlap your vision.
Rengar.build: Prioritize armor against Rengar's main damage. Rengar W Battle Roar is used for healing, so fit Executioner's Calling between your core items. While Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt reduces your armor, the armor you have built is also less effective.
Rengar.fight: Trade when Rengar's resource bar is empty and just after Rengar W Battle Roar is used. Dodge Rengar E Bola Strike, then close in with Graves E Quickdraw and keep attacking. Rengar has no skill to create distance on his own, so use Graves R Collateral Damage to adjust your position when you find an opening to engage.
Rengar.laning: When Rengar is out of sight, avoid paths beside brush and use a Control Ward to reveal it. Gank when the opponent is past the middle of the lane and your ally has a way to lock them down. If the angle is uncertain, clear camps for levels and gold; at camps with walls, use Graves Q End of the Line against the wall.
Rengar.combo: Dodge Rengar E Bola Strike and confirm that Rengar W Battle Roar is down, then close the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and attack at close range. Just before reloading, use Graves E Quickdraw to refill the magazine and keep attacking. Once close, cut off his vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and follow with Graves Q End of the Line; if Rengar has his back to a wall, aim at the wall to make the explosion hit quickly.
Rengar.escape: After Rengar throws Rengar E Bola Strike, you have an opening to go in with Graves E Quickdraw. If Rengar W Battle Roar is down and his resource bar is empty, there is less pressure to account for his healing and empowered ability. When chased, drop Graves W Smoke Screen behind you and, if needed, use the movement after casting Graves R Collateral Damage to cross a wall.
Rengar.phase: You get stronger as you stack, so if you survive the early game, the matchup against Rengar becomes more favorable over time. However, your range is short in the late game, making it dangerous to get caught first, so secure your early and mid-game gains with objectives and vision.
Rengar.teamfight: Do not start the fight from the front; watch for Rengar's engage from behind your allied frontline and within your vision. When Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt is active, stay with allies to overlap your detection range, and keep your backline from moving ahead of the frontline. After your allies draw the opponent's attention, go in from the side with Graves E Quickdraw, positioning so no other unit is between you and your target.

Sejuani.watch: Sejuani Q Arctic Assault knocks you up and Sejuani R Glacial Prison stuns you, so move to the side and dodge when you see their windups. If you are hit by the first strike of Sejuani W Winter's Wrath, get out of range before the second strike. Sejuani E Permafrost stacks can also build from attacks by nearby allied melee champions, so create distance when the stack indicator fills.
Sejuani.build: Prioritize magic resistance against Sejuani's main damage, and choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps.
Sejuani.laning: Gank when the opponent is pushed past the middle of the lane and your ally has a way to lock them down. If the angle is uncertain, do not force it; use Graves Q End of the Line against a wall to clear camps quickly and earn levels and gold.
Sejuani.combo: After Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and attack. Position so no other unit is between you and Sejuani, cut off her vision with Graves W Smoke Screen, then hit her with Graves Q End of the Line. If Sejuani has her back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line at the wall to make the explosion hit quickly.
Sejuani.escape: Right after you bait out Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is your chance to engage. After Sejuani E Permafrost stuns once, stacks cannot build again for a short time, giving you an opening, but create distance to avoid the empowered first attack right after the stun. Adjust your distance with Graves E Quickdraw and Graves R Collateral Damage.
Sejuani.phase: In the early and mid game, focus on securing your advantage in objectives and vision. If you survive the early game, Graves becomes more favorable over time, but in the late game his range is short and his magic resistance is low, so avoid being caught first by Sejuani's crowd control.
Sejuani.teamfight: Do not start the fight from the front. After your allies draw Sejuani's attention, engage from the side with Graves E Quickdraw. Stick close to the damage dealers while dodging Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and Sejuani R Glacial Prison, and maintain a position with no other unit between you and your target. Use Graves R Collateral Damage when you can line up another enemy behind the target you hit.

Shaco.watch: Watch for Shaco W Jack In The Box around unwarded brush and objectives, and check the area first with a Control Ward or Oracle Lens. Shaco Q Deceive empowers his first basic attack when he gets behind you, so if you think Shaco is nearby, keep your back to a wall or face your allies. When Shaco R Hallucinate’s clone dies, it leaves a box that explodes and fears nearby enemies, so move away immediately.
Shaco.build: Build magic resistance first to account for the magic damage from Shaco W Jack In The Box, Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison, and Shaco R Hallucinate. Choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps. Also build health so you don’t stay in the low-health range where Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison deals more damage.
Shaco.fight: Fight by closing the gap with Graves E Quickdraw right after Shaco uses Shaco Q Deceive. Graves’ basic attacks are blocked by the first unit they hit, so find an angle with no other units between you and Shaco. Don’t waste your damage on Shaco R Hallucinate’s clone; identify the real Shaco by watching health bar reactions.
Shaco.laning: Keep vision around your allied jungle entrances early to watch for Shaco’s ganks and invades. If there’s no clear gank angle, farm by casting Graves Q End of the Line against a camp wall. Check for nearby Shaco W Jack In The Box before starting an objective.
Shaco.combo: When Shaco Q Deceive is down, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks. Then use Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off vision and hit Graves Q End of the Line. If Shaco has his back to a wall, aim Graves Q End of the Line at the wall to trigger the explosion quickly. Just before reloading, use Graves E Quickdraw to load a shell and keep attacking.
Shaco.escape: The moment after Shaco uses Shaco Q Deceive is your chance to close the gap and catch him. Check for Shaco W Jack In The Box in unwarded areas first, and don’t blindly enter positions where you risk being feared. If Shaco appears in a teamfight with Shaco Q Deceive, focus him immediately with your allies.
Shaco.phase: Use Graves’ strength in the early and mid game to secure objectives and vision. If you buy time, Shaco’s ability to win isolated fights falls off later, but Graves also has short range and low magic resistance late, so avoid being caught first.
Shaco.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front. Wait for your allies to draw attention, then flank with Graves E Quickdraw. If Shaco enters with Shaco Q Deceive, focus him with your allies as soon as he appears. If you kill Shaco R Hallucinate’s clone, move away to avoid the explosion and fear it leaves behind.

Shyvana.watch: Avoid the slow and maximum-health damage from Shyvana E Molten Burst, and don’t stay close long enough to get hit by Shyvana Q Emberstrike. Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent is unstoppable while she flies, so don’t try to interrupt her engage; create distance from where she lands.
Shyvana.build: Buy Executioner's Calling between core items to counter the healing from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis. Choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps to account for the magic damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, Shyvana E Molten Burst, and Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent. Her basic attacks also deal physical damage, so armor is still valuable.
Shyvana.fight: Pressure Shyvana when her Fury bar is empty, and don’t rush into a head-on fight when it’s full. If Shyvana uses Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent to get on you, manage the distance with Graves E Quickdraw and avoid extended close-range fights where she can keep hitting you with Shyvana Q Emberstrike. Look for another chance to attack when Shyvana returns to human form and loses her bonus health and empowered abilities.
Shyvana.laning: It’s important to gain an advantage before Shyvana stacks Shyvana P Scalemail permanently. If there’s no clear gank angle, don’t force it; clear camps to gain levels and gold.
Shyvana.combo: When Shyvana’s Fury bar is empty or Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent is down, close in with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from an angle with no units between you and Shyvana. Just before reloading, use Graves E Quickdraw to load a shell, then cut off vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and hit Graves Q End of the Line. Against Shyvana with her back to a wall, fire Graves Q End of the Line against the wall, then finish with Graves R Collateral Damage.
Shyvana.escape: When Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent is down, she has no way to close the gap, so look for a chance to engage with Graves E Quickdraw. When Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent is available, don’t use Graves E Quickdraw to engage recklessly.
Shyvana.phase: In the mid game, turn Graves’ strength into objective and vision control, but don’t start an objective in front of Shyvana when her Fury bar is full. Shyvana gets stronger as she stacks, and Graves has short range and low magic resistance late, so avoid being caught first.
Shyvana.teamfight: Spread out so several allies aren’t hit together by Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent’s path and empowered area-of-effect abilities. Graves shouldn’t engage from the front; wait for allies to draw attention, then flank with Graves E Quickdraw. Keep a position with no units between you and your target, and use Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off vision and create an opening to attack.

Skarner.watch: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact passes through terrain, and being slammed into a wall after he grabs you stuns you, so don’t stand with your back to a wall. Graves E Quickdraw and R Collateral Damage cannot break the suppression from Skarner R Impale, so don’t enter his short range first.
Skarner.fight: After baiting out Skarner E Ixtal's Impact, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and follow up with basic attacks. Using Graves E Quickdraw toward an enemy champion can build more defensive stacks, and hitting them with a basic attack can reduce its cooldown. Keep close-range fights short so Skarner can’t keep hitting you with empowered basic attacks from Skarner Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval.
Skarner.laning: If there’s no clear gank angle, farm by casting Graves Q End of the Line against a camp wall. When ganking, approach with Graves E Quickdraw if the enemy is pushed forward and your ally can hold them, then place W Smoke Screen along their escape route.
Skarner.combo: When Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down, approach with Graves E Quickdraw and land basic attacks from an angle where units won’t block them. Then cut off vision with Graves W Smoke Screen and hit the explosion from Q End of the Line; if the enemy has their back to a wall, aim Q at the wall. Use Graves R Collateral Damage if you need to finish them.
Skarner.escape: The moment after Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down is your chance to engage with Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage. If Skarner R Impale is still available, be careful with your engage range, since you won’t be able to escape with a movement ability after being suppressed.
Skarner.teamfight: Graves shouldn’t start the fight. Wait for allies to draw attention, then flank with E Quickdraw and get beside the enemy carry. Position yourself so no units are between you and your target, and keep your distance from Skarner and his allies so you aren’t pulled deep into the enemy team by Skarner R Impale. You can be pulled over terrain at the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit, so don’t stand against a wall.

Taliyah.watch: Taliyah Q Threaded Volley can’t change direction while casting, so sidestep instead of approaching in a straight line. Don’t dash across worked ground with Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage.
Taliyah.build: Prioritize magic resistance against the magic damage from Taliyah Q Threaded Volley and E Unraveled Earth. Choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps to make up for Graves’ low magic resistance.
Taliyah.fight: If Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is on the ground, don’t cross it with Graves E Quickdraw; approach on foot or go around the worked ground. When closing in, find an angle with no other units between you and Taliyah so you can land basic attacks from Graves P New Destiny. If Taliyah has her back to a wall, hit the wall with Graves Q End of the Line to trigger the explosion quickly.
Taliyah.laning: Try to gank when Taliyah is pushed past the middle of her lane and your ally has a way to hold her. If the angle is unclear, use your fast jungle clear to farm camps and gain levels and gold. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, suspect she may use Taliyah P Rock Surfing and R Weaver's Wall to affect another lane, and back off in advance.
Taliyah.combo: Close the gap on a path without worked ground with Graves E Quickdraw, then stay close and land basic attacks. Follow with Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off Taliyah’s vision and hit her with Q End of the Line. Use Graves R Collateral Damage to finish her, but account for where it knocks you back after casting.
Taliyah.escape: Don’t engage with Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage if Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is on the ground or the area is where W Seismic Shove will land. If only one of Taliyah’s movement abilities is down, she can escape with the other, so look for an opening before R Weaver's Wall comes back. Once you have a route that avoids worked ground, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw or R Collateral Damage.
Taliyah.phase: Use your early and mid game strength to secure objectives and vision. This matchup favors Graves because his physical damage works well against Taliyah’s low armor, and the advantage grows as he scales. Late game, though, his short range and low magic resistance mean you should avoid being caught first.
Taliyah.teamfight: Graves shouldn’t engage from the front. Wait for allies to draw the enemy’s attention, then approach Taliyah from the flank or behind with E Quickdraw. Don’t dash through Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. Once close, keep a position with no units between you and Taliyah and land basic attacks.

Udyr.watch: Udyr E Blazing Stampede increases his movement speed as he closes in and stuns on the first hit. Udyr Q Wilding Claw and Udyr R Wingborne Storm deal damage based on your maximum health, so avoid staying in close combat for too long.
Udyr.build: Build armor first against Udyr’s physical damage. If Udyr survives through the healing from Udyr W Iron Mantle, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items. If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, choose Mercury’s Treads for boots.
Udyr.fight: Chip Udyr down before he gets close, but save Graves E Quickdraw for when he approaches. Once Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield expires, pressure him with basic attacks and Graves Q End of the Line so he has no chance to heal. Position yourself so no other unit is between you and Udyr, allowing your basic attacks to hit.
Udyr.laning: Place vision at jungle entrances and key paths to track Udyr’s movements. Don’t push forward in lane when Udyr is missing. If there’s no clear gank opportunity, farm camps to gain levels and gold.
Udyr.combo: After Udyr E Blazing Stampede is down, close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw and land point-blank basic attacks. Then use Graves W Smoke Screen to cut off his vision and hit him with Graves Q End of the Line. If Udyr has his back to a wall, fire Q along the wall. Use Graves R Collateral Damage if you need to finish him.
Udyr.escape: Right after you bait Udyr E Blazing Stampede, you have a chance to close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw or Graves R Collateral Damage. If Udyr E Blazing Stampede stuns you, retaliate or escape while that target can’t be stunned by it again for a while. If Udyr E Blazing Stampede is active again, watch out for the stun. When chased, cast Graves W Smoke Screen behind you to cut off the pursuer’s vision.
Udyr.phase: In the early and mid game, turn your lead from fast clears and skirmishes into objectives and vision. In the late game, avoid being caught first because of your short range and low magic resistance.
Udyr.teamfight: Don’t start the fight from the front. Wait until your allies draw the enemy’s attention, then enter from the flank or behind with Graves E Quickdraw. Target weak enemies in the back instead of forcing a fight against Udyr, who is tanky with defensive items and Udyr W Iron Mantle. Stay positioned so no other unit is between you and your target.

Vi.watch: Vi Q Vault Breaker deals more damage when fully charged, so when you see her charging, dodge sideways with Graves E Quickdraw. Vi W Denting Blows reduces armor and increases Vi’s attack speed the more she hits the same target, so don’t fight her for long. Vi R Cease and Desist follows its target all the way and knocks them up, so when Vi has R, stay with your allies and don’t wander out of vision.
Vi.build: Build armor first because Vi’s main damage is physical. Vi W Denting Blows reduces armor and deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone. Since basic attacks and attack speed are central to Vi’s damage, consider an option that lowers her attack speed as well.
Vi.fight: Take a short trade right after dodging or baiting Vi Q Vault Breaker. Close the gap with Graves E Quickdraw to build armor stacks, then land an empowered basic attack from Graves P New Destiny when no unit is between you and Vi. Don’t trade for long and let Vi W Denting Blows stack; create distance instead.
Vi.laning: If there’s no clear gank opportunity, farm camps to gain levels and gold.
